hints: Focus on what LiAlH4 does to a carboxylic acid group, it is a very strong reducing agent that goes all the way.
Remember that one $\text{-COOH}$ group becomes one $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ group, and here you have two $\text{-COOH}$ groups on the same molecule.
Count carbons and oxygens in the starting acid and check which product keeps the same 2-carbon skeleton with both carbons now as alcohols.
walkthrough:
**Recall what LiAlH4 does**

Great start, let's remember our reducing agents. $\text{NaBH}_4$ is gentle and cannot reduce carboxylic acids, but $\text{LiAlH}_4$ is powerful and reduces them fully to primary alcohols.

General rule:
$$\text{R-COOH} \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4} \text{R-CH}_2\text{OH}$$

**Apply it to both acid groups**

Now look at your starting material. Ethanedioic acid is $\text{HOOC-COOH}$, so it has two carboxylic acid groups joined together.

With excess $\text{LiAlH}_4$, both groups are reduced:
$$\text{HOOC-COOH} \xrightarrow{\text{excess LiAlH}_4} \text{HOCH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$$

**Name the product**

That product has 2 carbons, each bearing an $\text{-OH}$ group. That is $\text{CH}_2\text{OHCH}_2\text{OH}$, which is ethane-1,2-diol. The carbon-carbon bond is never broken in this reduction.

options.A: Ethanol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, is incorrect because it has only one oxygen and implies the C-C bond was broken or one $\text{-COOH}$ was lost. Reduction with LiAlH4 keeps the carbon skeleton intact, so both carbons remain oxygenated.
options.B: Ethane-1,2-diol, $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, is correct. Each $\text{-COOH}$ is reduced to $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ by excess LiAlH4, so the dicarboxylic acid gives the diol with the 2-carbon chain unchanged.
options.C: Ethanedial, $\text{OHC-CHO}$, is incorrect because aldehydes are only a partial reduction stage. LiAlH4 is too strong to stop there, it reduces acids and aldehydes all the way to primary alcohols.
options.D: Methane, $\text{CH}_4$, is incorrect because it would require complete cleavage of the C-C bond and loss of all oxygen. LiAlH4 is a reduction of functional groups, not a cracking of the carbon chain.
